label: Hypnotized by her own partner — worldwide sweep, part B (19 Nov 2026)

description: Worldwide all-media pass (19 Nov 2026 PT) for adult women hypnotized by their husband, fiancé or boyfriend, covering films, TV, soaps, short dramas, AI series, TikTok/Instagram and adult titles. records.title: The Taste of Tea (茶の味 / Cha no Aji)
records.meta: Feature film · Japan · Japanese · dir. Katsuhito Ishii · comedy-drama · Cannes 2004 selection
records.character: Yoshiko Haruno (Satomi Tezuka), wife of hypnotherapist Nobuo Haruno (Tomokazu Miura)
records.summary: Gentle family comedy about the Haruno family in rural Tochigi. Father Nobuo is a hypnotherapist who sometimes practises hypnosis on his own family; in one scene the adults, including his wife Yoshiko, are hypnotized while the children watch TV. Benign, comedic use of hypnosis, not coercive.
records.mechanism: husband practising hypnotherapy on family members (comic, benign)
records.already_married_note: Nobuo and Yoshiko are the married parents of the Haruno household.
records.kids_together_note: The couple already have two children together, teenage son Hajime and eight-year-old daughter Sachiko. No new child during the film.
records.kids_note: No children from a previous relationship; Hajime and Sachiko are the couple's own children.

sources.label: Midnight Eye review ('a hypnosis therapist who occasionally practices on his own family')
Japan on Film review ('the adults are hypnotized while the kids watch TV')

records.evidence: Wikipedia gives the family and Nobuo's hypnotherapist job; Midnight Eye and Japan on Film reviews describe him hypnotizing his own family, including the adults.
records.fit_note: Loose fit: the husband hypnotizes his wife, but in a benign, comedic way, not to control her.

records.title: The Untameable
records.meta: Silent feature film · USA · English intertitles · Universal · dir. Herbert Blaché · based on Gelett Burgess's novel The White Cat (1907)
records.summary: Engineer Chester Arnold notices that his fiancée Joy keeps switching into a cold, vampish personality called 'Edna'. He finds out that her physician, Dr. Copin, has been hypnotizing her to get her money, and that while under his influence she has been led into marrying him. Chester confronts Copin, and the doctor is fatally wounded when the maid releases Joy's hounds. Free of his influence, Joy goes back to her old self and to Chester.
records.hypnotist: her physician Dr. Copin, who becomes her husband through hypnosis
records.mechanism: doctor hypnotizes a wealthy woman into marrying him for her money
records.married: yes (to the hypnotist, while under his control)
records.already_married_note: She is engaged to Chester; the marriage to Copin happens while she is hypnotized.
records.pregnancy_note: No pregnancy in the copyright-record synopsis.
records.kids_together_note: No children with Copin (he dies) or with Chester in the synopsis.

sources.label: Wikipedia — The Untameable (plot from copyright record; AFI Catalog cited)

records.evidence: The Wikipedia plot, taken from the film's copyright record, states that Joy is hypnotized by Dr. Copin and induced to marry him.

records.title: Sea Change (Karen White novel)
records.meta: Novel (reading work) · USA · English · NAL Accent / Berkley (Penguin) · Southern gothic romance · ISBN 978-0451236760
records.character: Ava Whalen, 35-year-old midwife, newly married to child psychologist Matthew Frazier
records.summary: After a whirlwind courtship, Ava marries child psychologist Matthew Frazier and moves to his family home on St. Simons Island, Georgia. At Matthew's urging, she lets him hypnotize her to answer troubling questions about her past. Under hypnosis she recalls memories linking her to figures from the island's 18th-century history.

records.kids_together_note: The cited reviews and publisher text do not say.
